refutations.evidence: Reproduced script exactly: uniform +0.157%, time-aware +0.473%, delta +0.317%, 9/10 & 10/10 folds. DECOMPOSITION (exact): the entire +0.317% delta is the t0->t1 overnight gap on the 46% intraday subset. delta == overnight*(t5/t1) to machine precision; corr(delta,overnight)=0.9959. Intraday overnight gap mean +0.674% BUT median only +0.206% and share-positive only 53.4% (near coin-flip). FILL SENSITIVITY (extra slippage on the intraday close-fill / 단일가 auction): time-aware level 0bps +0.473% -> +10bps +0.426% -> +30bps +0.333% -> +50bps +0.239%; delta-positive folds drop 10->10->9->8. The median capturable overnight gap is +0.206% (low-price half +0.276%), which a single KOSDAQ tick/spread (10-30bps) can erase. LIQUIDITY TILT (adverse): drift is LARGEST in low-price (Q1 +0.819%) and KOSDAQ (+0.707% vs KOSPI +0.621%) names — exactly where the close-auction fill is least achievable. CAPACITY (decisive): CLAUDE.md mandates max_open_positions=1; holding is t0->T+5 (~5 business days). Single-position greedy execution takes only 187 of 1654 intraday signals (11%); 65% of active days have >1 simultaneous intraday event. Collision-pick fragility: greedy-random across 30 seeds ranges [+0.47%, +1.82%], and adversarial-worst collision pick = -1.23% mean / -0.84% median. Economics at max_order_value_krw=30000: ~+341 KRW/trade, ~37 trades/yr => ~+12,600 KRW (~$9)/yr. Coverage unbiased (matched +0.470% vs unmatched +0.472%); near-close 14:00-15:20 bucket still +0.62% so not a filing-time artifact.
refutations.reasoning: The mechanism is genuine and cleanly identified: the time-aware delta is 100% the event-day-close -> T+1-close overnight gap captured by entering one session earlier on intraday-published buybacks. It is NOT tail-driven (1/2/5% trimmed means hold at +0.63/0.61/0.56%; top 1% explains only 21%), coverage is unbiased, and the gross drift survives moderate slippage. So the edge is not fake. But the CLAIM is specifically that this is 'a durable, executable improvement worth pursuing toward live trading,' and on executability it fails the default-skeptical bar for three compounding reasons. (1) Fill-fragility on the very fill the mechanism requires: the median capturable gap is just ~20bps, smaller than a single KOSDAQ small-cap tick/spread, and the drift is concentrated precisely in the low-price/KOSDAQ names where transacting at the closing auction without moving it is least realistic; at +30bps extra entry slippage the delta halves and a fold flips. (2) Capacity is fatal under the project's own hard constraint max_open_positions=1 with a 5-day hold: only ~11% of intraday signals are reachable, and on the 65% of days with colliding signals the realized result swings from +1.8% to -1.2% purely on which name you happen to pick — i.e. the deployed P&L is dominated by selection luck the headline (trade-all-3562, no position limit) entirely ignores. (3) The absolute economics under max_order_value_krw=30000 are ~$9/yr — operationally not worth the live-execution risk. The headline +0.473%/+0.317% is a per-event statistical average over an un-constrained portfolio that cannot be held under the system's own risk limits. A real, mean-positive signal that is fill-fragile in exactly its dependent fill, undeployable under the 1-position cap, and selection-luck-dominated when constrained meets the refuted=true criteria (fold-survival is fine, but executability is not). Confidence 0.7 rather than higher because the gross/statistical effect is robust and unbiased — a different risk configuration (more concurrent positions, larger-cap-only filter, intraday-VWAP entry) could rehabilitate part of it; the refutation is specifically of the deploy-as-described claim.

refutations.evidence: Reproduced headline exactly: uniform +0.157%, time-aware +0.473%, delta +0.317%, 9/10 and 10/10 positive folds. DELTA robustness HOLDS: 10/10 folds positive at all three cutoffs (15:00 delta=+0.292%, 15:20=+0.317%, 15:25=+0.332%), min delta +0.102%/+0.083%/+0.118% in 2023H1, fold-level delta t=7.62; isolated intraday-only paired entry-timing gain +0.682% (median +0.212%), paired t=8.41. Matched 74% subset unbiased (uniform +0.157% matched vs +0.159% unmatched). BUT the ABSOLUTE time-aware level fails durability/executability: (1) Fat-tail dependence — median trade = -0.044% (loses), win rate exactly 50%, winners +4.87% vs losers -3.85%; mean excl top 1% trades = +0.167%, excl top 5% = -0.421% (flips negative); trades >+10% (2.3% of sample) contribute 203% of total PnL, trades >+15% (2.3%) contribute 111%. (2) Threshold fragility — clears +0.30% bar by only 0.17%; fold-level mean +0.477% std 0.470%, t vs +0.30% = 1.19 (not significant), 95% CI [+0.186%,+0.768%]; fold-block bootstrap P(mean<=+0.30%)=10.4%. (3) Slippage realism — model uses only 5bps/side; at 10bps mean=+0.373%, at 15bps mean=+0.273% (below bar, 8/10 folds), at 20bps +0.173% (6/10). 62% of intraday-tradable events are KOSDAQ (wider spreads at close auction). (4) Worst regime 2022H1 still -0.419% time-aware; mean excl top-2 folds (2026H1,2024H2) = +0.320% trade-weighted. (5) Capacity — 80% of active days have >1 event, max_open_positions=1 with 5-day hold captures only ~7% (~205 of 3562 signals); sequential single-position sim mean +1.150% but realized cumulative path drawdown -71.5% of one-trade notional. Cutoff/seed insensitive (delta stable), but the level is not.
refutations.reasoning: The entry-timing DELTA is genuinely durable and seed/cutoff-insensitive (10/10 folds, t=7.62, survives 15:00-15:25 cutoffs) — that part of the claim is correct and the mechanism (capturing the post-announcement same-day-close-to-next-close drift on intraday filings, mean overnight +0.674%) is real. However, the CLAIM under test is that the time-aware ENTRY is a durable, EXECUTABLE improvement worth pursuing toward live trading, and that absolute level fails three skeptical tests. First, the +0.473% mean is a positive-skew lottery, not a robust mean: the median trade loses (-0.044%), win rate is exactly 50%, and removing the top 5% of trades flips the strategy to -0.421%; 2.3% of trades produce >100% of all PnL. Those extreme winners are large up-moves (likely limit-up-adjacent names) you are least likely to fill at the closing auction you must transact in, so the very PnL the edge depends on is the most fill-fragile. Second, it clears the +0.30% bar by a statistically insignificant margin (fold t vs bar = 1.19; bootstrap 10.4% chance it is at/below the bar) and falls below the bar at 15bps/side slippage, which is conservative not aggressive for reaction-buying 62%-KOSDAQ names into a 10-minute closing auction. Third, the worst 6-month period is still -0.419% and capacity under the system's own max_open_positions=1 captures only ~7% of signals. Per the default posture, a thin, fat-tail-concentrated, fill-fragile, threshold-marginal edge is refuted as a durable executable improvement — even though the entry-timing insight itself is worth keeping and re-testing with realistic close-auction slippage and a capacity-aware sim before any live step.

refutations.evidence: Reproduced baseline exactly: always-trade time-aware +0.473%/trade, +0.317% delta, 9/10 folds (matched set 3,562 events). But "always-trade" assumes taking ALL 3,562 events = ~3.6 signals/business-day with a 5-trading-day hold. Under the config default max_open_positions=1, greedy first-come-first-served (signals in entry-day order, take only if a slot is free) takes just 194-237 of 3,562 signals = ONLY 5-7%. Per-trade realized is wildly unstable across reasonable modeling choices: event-date calendar -> take 5%, per-trade +0.012%, cum +2.3%; business-day calendar -> take 7%, per-trade +0.760%, cum +180%. To resolve this, ran Monte Carlo (N=400) randomizing the uncontrollable tie-break order and start phase: single-slot per-trade = median +0.255% (mean +0.250, p5 -0.295%, p95 +0.781%, std 0.323%); 55% of plausible execution paths land BELOW the claim's own +0.30%/trade bar, and 21% are <= 0. Multi-slot does not rescue it: max_open=3 -> take 19%, per-trade +0.067% (a ~7x collapse from +0.473%); max_open=5 -> take 31%, per-trade +0.283% (still below +0.30 bar). Throughput at 1 slot is ~227 trades over ~5 yrs = ~45 trades/yr.
refutations.reasoning: The headline edge is an "always-trade" statistic that is physically undeployable for a retail account: 3,562 buyback events arrive at ~1.6-3.6 per business day, but a 5-trading-day hold with the system's own configured max_open_positions=1 lets you hold at most one position at a time, so you can take only ~45 trades/year (~6% of signals). The surviving sample is selected by AVAILABILITY (which day you happen to be free), not by skill, and the claim itself concedes the selector adds ~0 lift. When I remove the arbitrariness in that availability draw via Monte Carlo over tie-break and phase, the realized single-slot per-trade is a median +0.255% with std +0.323% — the dispersion is as large as the mean, and a majority of execution paths fall short of the claim's +0.30% threshold with a meaningful tail of negative outcomes. The two point estimates (+0.012% vs +0.760%) that flip on a trivial calendar choice are just two samples from this wide, mostly-sub-threshold distribution, confirming fragility. Increasing slots to 3 or 5 lets you take more signals but the per-trade edge collapses 2x-7x (to +0.067% / +0.283%), never durably clearing the bar. The +0.317% entry-timing delta is real as a mechanism, but it cannot be harvested at scale by a single-position retail account: the capacity constraint is the single biggest haircut and it turns a clean +0.473%/trade, 9/10-fold result into a noisy ~+0.25% median that is below threshold most of the time and undeployable in practice. Not a durable, executable improvement worth pushing toward live trading as stated. (Note: this attack examined only capacity/concurrency; per-fold concentration and fill realism at the closing auction are additional, separate risks not credited here.)

refutations.evidence: Reproduced claim exactly: uniform +0.157%, time-aware +0.473%, delta +0.317%, 9/10 ta-positive, 10/10 delta-positive folds. COVERAGE BIAS (the core of my angle) FAILS: matched (3,562) vs unmatched (1,239) uniform-T+1 returns are statistically identical — +0.157% vs +0.159%, Welch p=0.99; per-fold matched-minus-unmatched diff averages only +0.036% (noisy, ranges -1.21% to +1.40%, no systematic direction). Coverage is 62-85% in EVERY fold (min 2024H2/2025H1 ~62%), unmatched events spread across all regimes, not concentrated. So the 74% subset is representative and NOT biased upward. CLASSIFICATION/FILL prong partially lands: the entire entry-timing delta is the t0_close->t+1_close overnight leg (+0.674% mean on intraday events, 53.4% positive); 23.9% of intraday events (395, =11.1% of matched) file in the tight 14:30-15:20 window and show the HIGHEST time-aware return (+1.448%), so the most fill-fragile events carry disproportionate weight. Stress-test tightening the realistic-fill cutoff degrades monotonically: 15:20->+0.473%, 15:00->+0.449%, 14:30->+0.394%, 14:00->+0.359% (still clears +0.30% bar, 10/10 delta folds), 13:00->+0.284% (BELOW bar). Boundary spot-check confirmed correct mechanical classification (15:18=intraday, 15:24=afterclose) and 78 events at 15:20-15:30 conservatively dropped to afterclose.
refutations.reasoning: My assigned attack — coverage and classification bias — does NOT refute the claim, so on this specific angle refuted=false. The selection-bias hypothesis is decisively rejected: matched and unmatched events have identical uniform returns (p=0.99) and coverage is balanced across all folds, so the matched subset is representative and the +0.157% uniform baseline is not inflated by the 26% missing events. The classification is also mechanically correct (intraday/after-close split at the 15:20 cutoff is applied without look-ahead, with a conservative 78-event miss at the closing-auction boundary). The one real weakness I surfaced is fill-realism concentration: ~24% of intraday events file in the tight 14:30-15:20 window and disproportionately drive the time-aware return, and the edge degrades to below the +0.30% bar (+0.284%) under an aggressive 13:00 cutoff. But under a defensible 14:00 cutoff the edge still holds at +0.359% with 10/10 positive delta folds, and the coverage/classification machinery itself is sound. So on this angle the claim survives — though I flag that the un-validatable closing-auction fill (no intraday price data exists to confirm executability against the t0_close) and the single-position capacity limit remain the unaddressed risks that a different attack angle (fill/slippage or capacity) should target. My confidence is moderate (0.6) because the edge clears the bar only with a generous reaction-time assumption.

synthesis.honest_summary: Two separate questions, two separate answers. (1) The entry-timing DELTA is genuinely robust: I reproduced the headline exactly (uniform +0.157%, time-aware +0.473%, delta +0.317%) and confirmed the delta is +0.29%-0.33% and positive in 10/10 folds at every cutoff (15:00/15:20/15:25), with the worst fold still non-negative. The mechanism is cleanly identified and not a fluke — the entire delta is the event-day-close to next-close overnight gap captured by buying one session earlier on intraday-published buybacks, coverage is unbiased (matched vs unmatched uniform returns identical, p=0.99), and the dedicated coverage/classification-bias attack failed to refute. So the time-aware insight itself is real and worth keeping. (2) The absolute LEVEL is not tradable today, for three compounding reasons that the headline (an unconstrained always-trade portfolio with no position limit) hides. It is a positive-skew lottery, not a robust mean: the median trade loses (-0.044%), win rate is 49.6%, and removing the top 5% of trades flips the strategy to -0.42% — the PnL lives in extreme up-moves that are the hardest to fill at the closing auction the mechanism requires. The required fill is fragile: the median capturable overnight gap is only ~20bps (smaller than one KOSDAQ small-cap tick), the drift concentrates in low-price/KOSDAQ names where the close-auction fill is least achievable, and +30bps of extra entry slippage halves the delta and flips a fold. And capacity is decisive: under the project's own max_open_positions=1 with a 5-day hold, only ~6% of signals (~41/yr) are reachable, Monte Carlo over tie-break/phase gives a median of only ~+0.25% with 55% of paths below the +0.30% bar and 21% at-or-below zero, and at the 30,000-KRW order cap the economics are ~$2-9/year. The delta is real; the deployable strategy as described is not.
synthesis.recommended_next_step: Build a capacity-aware, fill-realistic forward simulator before any live step: run the time-aware buyback signal in paper mode with the system's actual max_open_positions=1 (and a larger-cap/KOSPI-only or min-price filter to test the fill-fragility hypothesis), modeling the closing-auction entry with realistic per-name spread/tick slippage rather than the flat 5bps/side. The single most informative artifact is collecting real intraday/closing-auction fill prices for the next several months of live buyback events to validate whether the ~20bps median overnight gap is actually capturable at t0_close in the low-price/KOSDAQ names that carry the edge — that is the one un-validatable assumption no historical daily-close dataset can answer.
synthesis.pdf_paragraph: On the full buyback history (3,562 events with scraped filing times, 74% coverage, 10 half-year folds 2021H2-2026H1), assigning each event its earliest realistically-tradable entry raises the per-trade net return from the uniform-T+1 assumption (+0.157%/trade, 7/10 folds positive) to a time-aware level of +0.473%/trade (9/10 folds positive), an entry-timing delta of +0.317%/trade that is positive in 10/10 folds and stable at +0.29%-0.33% across 15:00/15:20/15:25 cutoffs. This delta is a real, robust effect: it is entirely the event-day-close to next-close overnight gap captured by buying one session earlier on intraday-published buybacks, and coverage is unbiased (matched vs unmatched uniform returns +0.157% vs +0.159%, p=0.99). However, the absolute time-aware level is not tradable today: the median trade loses (-0.044%), win rate is 49.6%, removing the top 5% of trades flips the mean to -0.42%, the median capturable overnight gap is only ~20bps (eroded below the +0.30% bar by ~30bps of slippage), and under the system's own max_open_positions=1 limit with a 5-day hold only ~6% of signals (~41/year) are reachable, yielding a capacity-realistic median of ~+0.25%/trade and ~$2-9/year at the 30,000-KRW order cap. Verdict: keep the entry-timing finding as a genuine, documented edge in the research, but do not advance this strategy to live trading at its current absolute level until a capacity-aware, closing-auction-fill-realistic forward test confirms the gap is actually capturable.
